summary: Root cause of the last two rejections was my reply format, not the product: the agent-turn harness requires the final message to be exactly the JSON envelope {submission, summary}, and my previous two replies had a sentence of prose before the JSON, so the harness failed to parse the response ('Expecting value: line 1 column 1'). The draft itself was never the problem and still preflights valid. Action=continue with one Candidate (disposition concrete_suspicion, preferred_check source_review, priority 1), now marked repair_of=3147be0f57714dcb86f042681a3fa814. Sourced observation: the TryPreAccept defer-cycle guard in handleTryPreAcceptReply is inert, because lb.possibleQuorum is initialized all-false and only ever assigned false (epaxos/epaxos.go:1445-1446) and the notInQuorum loop tests the constant lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] for every q instead of lb.possibleQuorum[q] (epaxos/epaxos.go:1461); notInQuorum is therefore always r.N and notInQuorum == r.N/2 cannot hold, so the block introduced by the in-source comment 'this is to prevent defer cycles' never runs. Principal fact F-RECOVERY-DECISION, direct behavior B-TPA-REPLY-LEADER, supporting B-RECOVERY-START / B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER / B-EXEC, activity_classes A3 with supported core activity A1. Counterevidence and unknowns keep the remaining premises open: handlePrepareReply's sub-case 4 predicate is textually identical to sub-case 3 (so TryPreAccept may be unreachable and the guard merely dead code), and executeCommands may retrigger recovery so a defer may not be permanent. The handlePreAccept wrong-row write (InstanceSpace[LeaderId]) remains a local anomaly, not a claimed defect, because no history producing Status>=ACCEPTED with Cmds==nil could be sourced. Preflight returns valid=true; formal acceptance and execution remain the controller's.
